programs.name: Equitable Energy Future Grant (EEF)
programs.statusNote: New NOFO being released by DCEO. Watch DCEO grant opportunities.
programs.detail: $250K–$1M. Seed and predevelopment funding for Equity Eligible Contractors and equity-building projects.

programs.name: Community Solar Energy Sovereignty Grant (CSES)
programs.statusNote: New NOFO being released by DCEO. Watch DCEO grant opportunities.
programs.detail: Up to $8.5M/yr. Predevelopment and development for community-owned solar. Municipalities and community organizations.

programs.name: Clean Energy Contractor Incubator
programs.statusNote: NOFO coming soon. Watch DCEO grant opportunities.
programs.detail: Business development, bonding and insurance support for small and equity eligible contractors.

programs.name: Clean Energy Primes Accelerator
programs.statusNote: NOFO coming soon. Watch DCEO grant opportunities.
programs.detail: Capital access and prime-contractor readiness for established equity eligible firms.

programs.name: Clean Jobs Workforce Hubs
programs.statusNote: Clean Jobs Workforce Network Program NOFO open. Applications due October 30, 2026.
programs.detail: Regional training and placement. Note: CEJA workforce training funding opportunities are closed; DCEO says check back fall 2026.

programs.name: Climate Works Pre-Apprenticeship
programs.statusNote: Climate Works Pre-apprenticeship Program NOFO open. Applications due October 30, 2026.
programs.detail: Pre-apprenticeship pipeline into building trades for clean energy work.

programs.name: Energy Transition Navigators
programs.statusNote: Energy Transition Navigator Program NOFO open. Applications due October 30, 2026.
programs.detail: Community outreach staff who connect residents and businesses to CEJA programs.

programs.name: Energy Transition Community Grants
programs.statusNote: NOFO coming soon. Watch DCEO grant opportunities.
programs.detail: For communities affected by plant or mine closure. Awards sized to property tax and job losses.

programs.name: Illinois Home Weatherization Assistance Program
programs.statusNote: Delivered year-round through local agencies. Federal WAP funded at $329M for FY26. Apply through your local community action agency.
programs.detail: Income-qualified weatherization and efficiency measures delivered through local agencies.

programs.name: CEJA Program Map
programs.detail: Live map of workforce hubs, contractor programs, EJ and R3 community layers.

programs.name: Illinois Shines (Adjustable Block)
programs.detail: Upfront lump-sum payment for 15 years of REC value. To participate you work through an Approved Vendor, or become one yourself. This link is the Approved Vendor and Designee requirements page. PY 2026-27 opened June 1, 2026 with a 1,000 MW initial allocation across Small DG, Large DG, Traditional Community Solar, CDCS and Public Schools.

programs.name: Illinois Solar for All
programs.statusNote: The state-funded program continues. The separate federal Solar for All award that would have expanded it was terminated in August 2025; courts vacated that termination in September 2026 but money has not resumed. Treat any federal expansion as unavailable.
programs.detail: Approved Vendors are qualified and vetted solar companies that play a pivotal role in Illinois Solar for All. No-upfront-cost solar for income-qualified households, non-profits and public facilities in or adjacent to environmental justice and income-eligible communities. Submitted on your behalf by an ILSFA Approved Vendor, not directly by you. Sub-programs include Residential Solar, Non-Profit & Public Facilities, and Community Solar.

programs.name: CRGA Energy Storage Procurement
programs.detail: 20-year Indexed Storage Credit contracts for standalone, utility-scale storage. Initial procurement conducted August 2026 targeting 1,038 MW, split between MISO Zone 4 and the PJM ComEd area; those projects must reach commercial operation by Dec 31, 2029. Procurements continue until 3,000 MW is committed by Dec 31, 2030. Bidders must meet the Minimum Equity Standard and Prevailing Wage Act and execute a Project Labor Agreement.

programs.name: CRGA Implementation Hub
programs.detail: Public Act 104-0458, signed Jan 8, 2026, effective June 1, 2026. The IPA's implementation hub, updated as work progresses: storage procurement, Storage for All evaluation, virtual power plants, expanded efficiency, thermal energy, and the state's first Integrated Resource Plan, due to the ICC by Nov 15, 2026.

programs.name: C-PACE Financing
programs.detail: Long-term financing repaid through a voluntary property assessment. Up to 25% of property value. Existing buildings and new construction. Not available to government-owned property, which includes public community college and university campuses.

programs.name: Climate Bank Finance / SSBCI Loan Participation
programs.detail: Loans $25K–$2M covering 25–50% of project cost. Interest bought down to 2% max, 1% for socially and economically disadvantaged and very small businesses. Applied through an enrolled lender, not directly.

programs.name: Climate Bank Financing Directory
programs.detail: All Climate Bank programs sorted by who you are: residents, developers and contractors, local governments and nonprofits, municipal and cooperative utilities.

programs.name: Federal Funding Programs (Grid Resilience, EE Revolving Loan Fund)
programs.detail: Includes the DOE Grid Resilience State formula allocation and the Energy Efficiency Revolving Loan Fund capitalization.

programs.name: DG / EE Measures / EV Installer Certification
programs.statusNote: Rolling. EE Measures recertification due June 1 each year.
programs.detail: Required before a contractor can install for others or touch utility incentive money. Rolling applications. EE Measures recertification due June 1 annually.

programs.name: Equitable Energy Upgrade Program
programs.statusNote: Still in ICC rulemaking (Docket 25-0863) as of October 8, 2026. No tariff in effect.
programs.detail: Tariffed on-bill program. Still in rulemaking (Docket 25-0863). Delivered through utility tariffs, not directly by ICC. Do not build a capital stack on it yet.

programs.name: ComEd Energy Efficiency (Business & Residential)
programs.detail: Prescriptive and custom incentives, free assessments, instant discounts, small business direct install. Part of the ICC-approved 2026-2029 plan. ComEd serves northern Illinois only: roughly Iroquois County and I-80 north to Wisconsin, Iowa border to Indiana border. If your electric bill does not say ComEd, this is not your program.

programs.name: Ameren Illinois Energy Efficiency
programs.detail: Standard and custom business incentives, retro-commissioning, income-qualified programs. Ameren Illinois serves central and southern Illinois, about 1.2 million electric and 800,000 gas customers across 40,000 square miles. Not available in ComEd territory.

programs.name: Nicor Gas Energy Efficiency
programs.detail: Gas efficiency rebates, public sector custom incentives and on-bill financing. CRGA lets Nicor, Peoples and North Shore pursue increased energy reduction goals. Nicor serves most of the northern third of Illinois but NOT the city of Chicago, which is Peoples Gas.

programs.name: Peoples Gas / North Shore Gas Energy Efficiency
programs.detail: Gas efficiency rebates and direct-install programs. Peoples Gas serves the city of Chicago; North Shore Gas serves the northern suburbs in Cook and Lake counties. If you are in Chicago, this is your gas utility, not Nicor.

programs.name: MidAmerican Energy Efficiency Programs
programs.detail: Electric and gas efficiency rebates for the Illinois communities MidAmerican serves, mainly the Quad Cities area including Rock Island and Moline. Neither ComEd nor Ameren serves these customers.

programs.name: Virtual Power Plant Programs (CRGA)
programs.detail: New under CRGA. Pays households and businesses for smart thermostats, solar, small batteries and EVs dispatched at peak. Utilities filed program details June 1, 2026.

programs.name: Multifamily Retrofit & Preservation Financing
programs.statusNote: IHDA financing is offered through rounds and rolling programs. Confirm the current round with IHDA.
programs.detail: Layered financing for affordable multifamily including energy retrofits and new all-electric construction.

programs.name: Electric Vehicle Rebate Program
programs.statusNote: FY27 cycle open August 1 to December 31, 2026. $14M appropriated; rebates paid as funds allow. Apply within 180 days of purchase.
programs.detail: $2,000 per eligible new or used EV, plus $2,000 more for low-income applicants. Vehicle price under $80,000. Application cycle OPEN August 1 – December 31, 2026. Apply within 180 days of purchase.

programs.name: EV Charging & Transportation Infrastructure
programs.statusNote: Illinois resumed NEVI awards after the 2025 federal freeze was lifted by court order. Confirm the next round with IDOT.
programs.detail: NEVI corridor charging and related transportation infrastructure grants.

programs.name: Section 48E Clean Electricity Investment Credit
programs.detail: 30% base credit. The July 4, 2026 begin-construction deadline has passed. Projects that started by then have until Dec 31, 2030. Everything starting now must be PLACED IN SERVICE by Dec 31, 2027. Foreign entity sourcing rules apply.

programs.name: Elective Pay (Direct Pay)
programs.statusNote: Still available to tax-exempt owners. Solar and wind starting construction after July 4, 2026 must be placed in service by December 31, 2027. Geothermal and storage run into the 2030s.
programs.detail: Lets nonprofits, churches, municipalities and other tax-exempt owners receive 48E as a cash payment. This is the single most under-used tool in the CBO and municipal stack.

programs.name: 48E for Standalone Storage
programs.detail: Battery storage not co-located with solar is NOT subject to the accelerated solar and wind deadlines. Its longer runway is why storage is the strongest 2027–2030 play.

programs.name: Section 25D Residential Credit
programs.statusNote: Terminated for expenditures after December 31, 2025.
programs.detail: Ended December 31, 2025 with no step-down. Any client still budgeting a 30% homeowner credit has a hole in their pro forma.

programs.name: Rural Energy for America Program (REAP)
programs.statusNote: USDA rescinded the FY2025-2027 REAP funding notice on April 15, 2026. A new REAP rule takes effect October 16, 2026; a new funding notice with application windows has not been published. Under the new rule, ground-mount solar or wind on cropland is ineligible and projects must be completed before applying. Do not budget REAP until the new notice is out.
programs.detail: Grants and loan guarantees for rural small businesses and agricultural producers doing efficiency or renewables.

programs.name: DCEO Grant Opportunities — search all programs
programs.detail: Every open DCEO NOFO, not just energy. Grocery initiative, community development, infrastructure, small business — these often cover the capital and construction lines that energy programs will not.

programs.name: Office of Employment & Training — WIOA & regional workforce
programs.detail: Regional Workforce Managers, WIOA-funded training dollars, Apprenticeship Illinois and Job Training Economic Development. This is how a client staffs the project once it is funded.

programs.name: Illinois workNet — local workforce board finder
programs.detail: Find the Local Workforce Innovation Area and American Job Center that serves the client's county. First call for hiring, training dollars and on-the-job training contracts.

programs.name: Office of Entrepreneurship, Innovation & Technology — small business assistance
programs.detail: Small Business Development Centers, Business Information Center, procurement and certification help. The office that gets a contractor bid-ready and a small business bankable.

programs.name: Advantage Illinois — low-interest loan programs
programs.detail: Participation loans and credit enhancement for Illinois small businesses. Pairs with IFA SSBCI on the debt line of a capital stack.

programs.name: Illinois Works — bid credit & contractor resources
programs.detail: Bid credit program and apprenticeship resources for contractors on public works. Relevant to any project carrying prevailing wage or PLA requirements.

programs.name: Energy Efficiency & Conservation Block Grant (EECBG)
programs.statusNote: Final IEPA EECBG round awarded August 2025. No new funding announced. Do not budget it.
programs.detail: DOE/IIJA money for municipal and county strategic energy plans, energy audits and publicly owned building upgrades. Awards ran $50K–$250K. Final round was awarded August 2025 — watch for reauthorization before you budget it. Applicant must be a unit of local government. Schools, school districts and community college districts are not eligible — partner with your municipality, which must be the applicant.

programs.name: Office of Energy — codes training, assessments & trust funds
programs.statusNote: IEPA Office of Energy page lists the Efficient & Resilient Public Buildings Grant ($50K-$200K, local governments, DOE State Energy Program funds) but shows it as both open and closed. Confirm with IEPA before referring.
programs.detail: Energy Code training and technical support, wastewater treatment plant energy assessments, and the Energy Efficiency Trust Fund for low-income and government facilities.

programs.name: Electric School Bus & fleet programs
programs.statusNote: US EPA Clean School Bus is being revamped; no open round as of October 2026 and EPA says new funding details come "later in 2026." IEPA VW school bus rounds are awarded. For fleet trucks see Driving a Cleaner Illinois VW Round 9.
programs.detail: Replacement funding for diesel school buses and public fleet vehicles, prioritizing environmental justice areas.

programs.name: GRID — grid resilience for municipal utilities & co-ops
programs.detail: DOE 40101(d) grid resilience grants distributed by the Climate Bank. Award range roughly $150,000 to $8,000,000. Built for small utilities and disadvantaged communities.

programs.name: Small Utility Clean Energy Planning Grant
programs.detail: CPRG-funded planning money for municipal and cooperative utilities: technical assessments, procurement strategy and PPA readiness. Rolling application plus competitive rounds.

programs.name: Stretch Energy Code adoption support
programs.detail: Helps municipalities adopt, implement and enforce the Illinois Stretch Energy Code — staff time, training and legal review.

program.label: Climate Bank — Stretch Code Adoption Support

programs.name: Federal Tax Credit / REC Bridge Loan
programs.statusNote: Not on the Climate Bank's current program list (checked October 8, 2026). Confirm with IFA before using.
programs.detail: Short-term financing that covers the gap between paying for a project and receiving the federal credit through elective pay, or the Illinois Shines REC payment.

programs.name: Energy Sovereignty Loan
programs.statusNote: Not on the Climate Bank's current program list (checked October 8, 2026). Confirm with IFA before using.
programs.detail: Low-cost debt supporting community ownership of clean energy assets rather than third-party ownership.

programs.name: Community Resilience Hubs & Community Charging
programs.statusNote: Not on the Climate Bank's current program list (checked October 8, 2026). Confirm with IFA before using.
programs.detail: Backup power and solar-plus-storage at community facilities, and publicly accessible EV charging in underserved areas.

programs.name: NEVI, Carbon Reduction, CMAQ & Freight-Port Infrastructure
programs.detail: Four federal formula and competitive programs a village or county can use for corridor charging, fleet depots, congestion and air quality projects, and freight infrastructure.

programs.name: Net metering & distributed generation rules
programs.detail: Retail-rate net metering for systems up to 2 MW, plus the DG installer certification your contractor must hold. Sets what the solar actually earns on the bill.

programs.name: Clean Building Navigator & Concierge (CPRG)
programs.detail: Outreach, intake, contractor coordination and project navigation for residents and small businesses pursuing electrification and efficiency upgrades.

programs.name: Green Resilient Retrofit & Energy Efficiency Program
programs.statusNote: If this relies on HUD GRRP: HUD restructured GRRP effective March 1, 2026 (awards converted to loans, solar and EV chargers no longer fundable). Confirm with IHDA what remains available.
programs.detail: Retrofit and resilience financing for affordable multifamily housing — relevant when a municipality or CBO controls housing stock.

programs.name: Industrial Assessment Center — UIC
programs.detail: DOE-funded program pairing trained staff and students to conduct free energy and pollution assessments at mid-size industrial facilities. UIC is Illinois' center, one of 28 nationally.

programs.name: Private Activity Bonds
programs.detail: Tax-exempt financing for 501(c)(3) organizations and other conduit borrowers to finance or refinance capital expenditures, including clean energy assets.

programs.name: Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund (GGRF)
programs.statusNote: Two tracks, both unresolved. NCIF/CCIA: en banc D.C. Circuit upheld the injunction August 4, 2026; the government is seeking Supreme Court review. Solar for All: termination vacated by federal courts in Rhode Island (Sept. 18, 2026) and D.C. (late Sept. 2026), but funds were not flowing as of October 7 and EPA is weighing appeal. Do not count on this in a capital stack.
programs.detail: Federal program funding clean energy and climate projects in low-income and disadvantaged communities. Solar for All Expansion and National Clean Investment Fund instruments are in litigation with funding paused — confirm current status before counting on this.

programs.name: Energy Efficiency Trust Fund Grant Program
programs.statusNote: FY26 round closed (first-come, first-served through June 30, 2026). $50K-$1M with match. Watch for the next IEPA NOFO.
programs.detail: Funds residential energy efficiency projects for public housing authorities, local governments, or nonprofit organizations.

programs.name: Energy Efficiency Assessment Program
programs.statusNote: FY26 round closed (through March 31, 2026). $5K-$60K, first-come, first-served. Watch for the next IEPA NOFO.
programs.detail: Grant funding for public housing authorities, local governments, or nonprofit organizations to assess energy efficiency opportunities before committing to a project.

programs.name: Energy Benchmarking & Efficiency at Community Colleges
programs.statusNote: Delivered through IGEN to member colleges, not by open application. No current application window posted. Confirm with IGEN.
programs.detail: Technical assistance and implementation funding to benchmark energy use and complete efficiency upgrades at Illinois community colleges. Delivered through the Illinois Green Economy Network (IGEN), not by direct application to IEPA. Prior awards ran about $106,000 per college, with priority to financially constrained institutions.

programs.name: REV Illinois Act
programs.detail: Reimagining Energy and Vehicles in Illinois Act — a highly competitive incentive program for manufacturers of EVs, EV components, and renewable energy equipment locating or expanding in Illinois.

programs.name: Charging & Fueling Infrastructure Grant
programs.detail: Federal discretionary grant for publicly accessible EV charging and alternative fueling infrastructure, with a rural and community set-aside.

programs.name: Driving a Cleaner Illinois
programs.statusNote: VW Round 9 (all-electric Class 4-8 local freight trucks, up to $18M) open until funds run out. CEJA EV Charging Round 3 closed. No open DERA NOFO. Checked October 8, 2026.
programs.detail: Funded by the Volkswagen settlement and federal DERA dollars. Covers charging station infrastructure and other mobile-source electrification projects, including publicly accessible charging.

programs.name: Returning Resident Clean Jobs Training Program
programs.detail: CEJA program delivering clean jobs training inside Illinois Department of Corrections facilities to individuals within 36 months of release, and post-release support into employment.

programs.name: Become an Equity Eligible Contractor (EEC)
programs.detail: Certification path for Approved Vendors, Designees and Subcontractors majority-owned by an Equity Eligible Person under CEJA. EEC status is the gateway credential for CEJA contractor money and for Illinois Shines and ILSFA equity set-asides. Vendor login is separate, at portal.illinoisabp.com.

programs.name: Energy Equity Portal
programs.detail: The IPA's hub for the clean energy workforce. Register as a clean energy company, post jobs, and connect with job seekers. Also hosts the Small & Emerging Business Hub.

programs.name: Small and Emerging Businesses in Illinois Solar for All and Illinois Shines
programs.detail: New for Program Year 2026-27. One registration covers both Illinois Shines and ILSFA. 'Small' means independently owned with under $4M gross revenue last year; 'emerging' means authorized to do business for under 3 years. Benefits include a lower batch threshold for project submittal, plus project selection preference and a collateral deduction on REC payments in ILSFA. Single Project Approved Vendors are not eligible.

audience.label: Illinois Shines — Become an AV or Designee (SEB)
Illinois Solar for All — Vendor Home

programs.name: SBA 504 Loans
programs.detail: Long-term, fixed-rate financing for major fixed assets — real estate, equipment — that promote business growth. Usable for clean energy retrofits bundled into a larger capital project.

programs.name: Charitable Trust Grant
programs.detail: General economic development funding for nonprofits. Not clean-energy specific, but usable for a CBO's broader capital campaign.

programs.name: Fleet Electrification Financing
programs.detail: Climate Bank debt product for converting municipal, business or nonprofit vehicle fleets to electric.

programs.name: Standard Offer Lease-to-Own
programs.statusNote: Not on the Climate Bank's current program list (checked October 8, 2026). Confirm with IFA before using.
programs.detail: Lets a homeowner or small nonprofit access solar or efficiency upgrades with no upfront cost, paying down to ownership over time.

programs.name: Carbon Free Schools
programs.statusNote: Not on the Climate Bank's current program list (checked October 8, 2026). Confirm with IFA before using.
programs.detail: Financing and technical support for Illinois school districts pursuing solar, storage and efficiency upgrades. K-12 school districts only. Community colleges are governed by the Public Community College Act, not the School Code.

programs.name: Working Capital Loan
programs.detail: Short-term operating capital for contractors and small businesses carrying a clean energy project through to payment.

programs.name: Building Electrification Financing
programs.statusNote: Not on the Climate Bank's current program list (checked October 8, 2026). Confirm with IFA before using.
programs.detail: Climate Bank debt product specifically for heat pump and all-electric conversion projects.

programs.name: Contractor Portal
programs.detail: Climate Bank's intake tool for contractors to access financing products and track applications.

programs.name: Federal Funds for Future Jobs (4FJ) Procurement
programs.detail: IFA procurement and technical assistance pathway connecting contractors to federal clean energy job opportunities.

programs.name: ILSFA Bright Neighborhoods Initiative
programs.statusNote: Initiative closed.
programs.detail: An Illinois Solar for All pilot, not Illinois Shines. Tested a consolidated model where the Program Administrator recruited participants directly and matched them to one pre-selected Approved Vendor. Ran in program years 2023-24 and 2024-25 in West Garfield Park and the West Side of Chicago, Waukegan, and the Carbondale-Marion area. Applications are closed; this link is the findings report. Watch for elements of it folding into the main ILSFA program.

programs.name: DOE Loan Programs Office / SEFI Partnership
programs.statusNote: Not on the Climate Bank's current program list (checked October 8, 2026). Confirm with IFA before using.
programs.detail: Illinois Climate Bank is a designated State Energy Financing Institution, which gives Illinois projects access to DOE Loan Programs Office credit support on large clean energy deals.

programs.name: Enabling Upgrades for Solar
programs.statusNote: Not on the Climate Bank's current program list (checked October 8, 2026). Confirm with IFA before using.
programs.detail: Covers the electrical panel and service upgrades a building sometimes needs before solar can be installed — a common hidden cost that stalls a project.

programs.name: Solar Training Pipeline Program
programs.detail: Established under the Future Energy Jobs Act (FEJA), now continued through DCEO. Builds a pool of trained solar installers, with priority for foster care alumni and returning citizens. Feeds into Illinois Solar for All projects.

programs.name: Craft Apprenticeship Program
programs.detail: FEJA-established program administered with IBEW to place solar and electrical trades training inside existing union apprenticeship programs statewide.

programs.name: Multicultural Jobs Program
programs.statusNote: Listed as a rolling DCEO opportunity (Future Energy Jobs Act Multi-Cultural) as of October 8, 2026.
programs.detail: FEJA-established program funding diversity-focused community organizations to deliver clean energy job training, sales and business-expansion support.

programs.name: Juntos Crecemos Grant Program
programs.detail: $10,000 grants for woman-owned food and beverage small businesses nationwide. Not clean-energy specific — general small business capital.

programs.name: Pillars of Giving
programs.detail: Nicor's charitable program supporting education, workforce and technical/vocational training aligned with its service territory.

programs.name: Community Empowerment Program
programs.detail: Youth-focused community grants. Not clean-energy specific — relevant if a CBO's clean energy work is bundled with a youth or community facility.

programs.name: Fall Awards
programs.detail: Grants for nonprofits and small businesses across education, workforce development, housing and economic development.

programs.name: Hometown Grants
programs.detail: Capital grants for small-town community development projects nationwide, open to local government and nonprofit applicants.

programs.name: Mission Sustainability Initiative Grants
programs.detail: Capacity-building and strategic planning grants for Illinois nonprofits — useful for a CBO building the organizational capacity to run a clean energy program.

programs.name: Spark Good Local Grants
programs.detail: Local cash grants from nearby Walmart stores and distribution centers for community, youth and education projects.

programs.name: Business & Industry Loan Guarantees
programs.detail: USDA guarantees a commercial lender's loan to a rural business: 85% on requests under $5M, 80% at $5M and up (FY2026). Terms up to 40 years. Covers buildings, land, equipment, machinery, inventory and some refinancing. Rural means outside cities over 50,000. Applied through your lender.

programs.name: Rural Business Development Grants
programs.statusNote: FY26 window closed June 30, 2026. Next cycle expected spring 2027.
programs.detail: Grants to public bodies and nonprofits that help small rural businesses: technical assistance, training, feasibility, revolving loan capital. No cost share. Smaller requests get priority. For-profits cannot apply directly.

programs.name: Value-Added Producer Grants
programs.statusNote: FY26 window closed April 22, 2026. Next window expected early 2027.
programs.match: 1:1 match (at least 50% of total project cost)
programs.detail: Up to $50K for planning (feasibility, business plans) or $200K for working capital to process and market a value-added agricultural product. Match must be spent before each reimbursement.

programs.name: Community Facilities Direct Loan & Grant
programs.detail: Loans and grants for essential community facilities in rural places of 20,000 or fewer: public buildings, schools, health care, public safety, utility services. Grants cover 15% to 75% of cost depending on population and income. Applications year-round.

programs.name: Rural Energy Savings Program
programs.statusNote: Open first-come, first-served until funds run out.
programs.detail: 0% loans for up to 20 years to electric co-ops and rural utilities, which relend to their members at up to 5% for efficiency, renewables and storage. Consumers do not apply to USDA; ask your co-op if it participates.

programs.name: Biorefinery, Renewable Chemical & Biobased Product Manufacturing Assistance (9003)
programs.statusNote: Accepted year-round with two decision cycles. Next: letter of intent by March 1, Phase 1 by April 1, 2027. Updated rule published July 9, 2026.
programs.detail: Loan guarantees up to $250M for building or retrofitting facilities that make advanced biofuels, renewable chemicals or biobased products with new technology.

programs.name: Advanced Biofuel Payment Program
programs.statusNote: Enrollment open October 1-31, 2026.
programs.detail: Production payments to producers of advanced biofuel made from renewable biomass other than corn kernel starch. Blenders do not qualify.

programs.name: Wood Innovations Grants
programs.statusNote: FY26 round closed April 22, 2026.
programs.detail: Expands markets for wood products and wood energy, including mass timber and wood energy feasibility.

programs.name: Community Wood Grants
programs.statusNote: FY26 round closed April 22, 2026.
programs.match: Federal share capped at 35% of capital cost (50% in special cases)
programs.detail: Capital grants for thermally led community wood energy systems and innovative wood product facilities.

programs.name: EDA Public Works & Economic Adjustment Assistance
programs.statusNote: Rolling, no deadline, until a new notice is issued or funds run out.
programs.detail: Infrastructure and economic recovery grants for distressed areas: industrial sites, rail spurs, utilities, workforce facilities. Applicant is a public body, nonprofit or college, not a private business.

programs.name: DRA States' Economic Development Assistance Program
programs.statusNote: 2026 round closed July 31, 2026. Annual.
programs.detail: Infrastructure, workforce and business development grants in the 16 Illinois DRA counties: Alexander, Franklin, Gallatin, Hamilton, Hardin, Jackson, Johnson, Massac, Perry, Pope, Pulaski, Randolph, Saline, Union, White, Williamson.

programs.name: Brownfields Assessment, Cleanup & RLF Grants
programs.statusNote: FY27 solicitations expected fall 2026, due about 60 days after release. No multipurpose grants in FY27.
programs.detail: Assessment up to $500K (coalitions up to $1M), cleanup up to $500K, revolving loan funds up to $1M. Clears contaminated sites for redevelopment, including clean energy siting.

programs.name: EDGE Tax Credit
programs.detail: Income or withholding tax credits for a business that adds jobs in Illinois when the project would not happen here otherwise. 50% of new-hire withholding, 25% for retained jobs, more in underserved areas. Small firms (100 or fewer) need the lesser of 5% growth or 50 jobs.

programs.name: Enterprise Zones
programs.detail: Inside a designated zone: 6.25% state sales tax exemption on building materials, 0.5% investment tax credit, local property tax abatement. Larger projects can get machinery and utility tax exemptions. Ask the local zone administrator.

programs.name: High Impact Business designation
programs.detail: Enterprise-zone-style tax exemptions for very large investments outside a zone, including qualifying wind, solar and storage facilities. Thresholds are high; this is for utility-scale and major manufacturing projects.

programs.name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG)
programs.statusNote: Economic Development and Community Revitalization are rolling. Public Infrastructure and Housing Rehab are annual competitive rounds.
programs.detail: HUD money for non-entitlement (mostly rural) Illinois communities: public infrastructure ($25M in 2026), housing rehab, community revitalization and economic development. Applicant is the local government.

programs.name: IDOA food and farm infrastructure grants
programs.statusNote: No energy-specific IDOA grant found October 8, 2026. Check each program page for the current round.
programs.detail: Resilient Food Systems Infrastructure, Local Food Infrastructure and Specialty Crop Block Grants fund processing, aggregation and value-added equipment for small farms and food businesses.

programs.name: OSLAD park grants
programs.statusNote: FY27 round closed August 31, 2026. Annual.
programs.detail: Park acquisition (up to $1.125M) and development (up to $600K) for local governments. Relevant when a park building or site upgrade includes efficiency or solar. School districts are not eligible.

programs.name: Illinois brownfields: cleanup loans and free site assessments
programs.statusNote: No posted deadline. Confirm loan funds are available with IEPA.
programs.detail: Brownfields Cleanup Revolving Loan Fund: low or no interest loans for municipally owned sites with an approved remedial plan. Targeted Brownfield Assessments: free soil and groundwater testing for communities.

programs.name: State Revolving Fund (water & wastewater loans)
programs.statusNote: Projects are funded from the annual Intended Use Plan list. Get on the project priority list first.
programs.detail: Low-interest loans for drinking water and wastewater systems, including energy efficiency at treatment plants. Applicant is the local government or utility.

programs.name: First-Time Farmer Bond
programs.statusNote: Lender-driven. Confirm with IFA or your lender.
programs.detail: Lower-rate loan through your own lender for a first-time farmer buying land, farm buildings or new equipment. Net worth up to $500K. Individuals only.

programs.name: Heavy Duty Charging Loans
programs.statusNote: Accepting initial intake submissions. Email climatebank@il-fa.com.
programs.detail: $10M CPRG-funded loan program for medium and heavy-duty fleet charging: depots, corridor hubs and grid upgrades. Fleets, charge operators, municipalities, schools and nonprofits.

programs.name: Community Geothermal Planning + Pilots
programs.statusNote: Phase One (planning) closed. Phase Two construction solicitation not yet open.
programs.detail: $16M CPRG program. Phase One planning $100K-$250K; Phase Two construction $1M-$5M for shovel-ready community geothermal.

programs.name: CEJA Primes Accelerator Loan Program
programs.statusNote: Not accepting applications as of October 8, 2026.
programs.detail: Low-interest working capital for contractors who completed the CEJA Primes Accelerator: payroll, supplies, inventory, equipment, vehicles.

programs.name: Energy Efficiency Revolving Loan Fund (bridge loans)
programs.statusNote: Pre-applications open.
programs.detail: 12-18 month bridge loans up to $3M while a project waits on elective pay, tax credits or incentives. Existing commercial buildings (incl. 5+ unit multifamily) with an energy audit from the last 5 years. No new construction.

programs.name: IMEA Electric Efficiency Program
programs.detail: $1M a year in incentives for business and public customers of IMEA's 32 member municipal electric systems: LED lighting, compressed air, refrigeration, variable speed drives, custom projects. Residential offers vary by town.

programs.name: Small Business Improvement Fund (SBIF)
programs.statusNote: 2026 round closed August 30, 2026. Rounds open by TIF district.
programs.detail: Reimbursement grants for permanent building improvements in eligible Chicago TIF districts, including HVAC, electrical, windows and roofs. Not competitive; meet the rules and you are funded.

programs.name: Community Development Grant / Neighborhood Opportunity Fund
programs.statusNote: Rounds announced periodically; a $42.5M round was awarded June 2026. Check Chicago.gov for the next deadline.
programs.detail: Grants for commercial corridor projects: storefront rehab, community centers, job training facilities, building reuse on the South, West and Southwest sides.

programs.name: Cook County Sun and Save
programs.statusNote: Program ran through August 31, 2026 or until funds ran out.
programs.detail: ARPA-funded residential solar subsidy for owner-occupied homes of 1-4 units with income between 80% and 120% of area median.
